steps.message:
# Ship is damaged when performing the action shown in the recording

### What happens
`recording.mp4` shows a ship performing an action at a station. The action does not
go the way it is set up to go, and the ship does not come out of it unharmed.
The collision outlines of the ship and the pad already overlap while the ship sits still, although the video shows it resting clear of the pad. A ship that really lands on a pad must still be caught by it, and the ship's overall shape must stay as it is.

### Expected
Performing the action shown in the recording must not damage the ship at all, at the spot shown in
the video or at any other equivalent spot of the same station. The hull-integrity readout stays at
100% for the whole action.

## Attached visual evidence

- `/app/.harbor_assets/recording.mp4`

You can inspect the video frame by frame with `ffmpeg` (installed in the image), e.g. extracting
still frames at specific timestamps to look closely at the HUD and the ship.

Inspect the attached file before making changes. The video describes observable behavior; it does
not prescribe source files, internal names, or an implementation strategy.

steps.message:
I've fixed it, but I couldn't watch the recording: `.harbor_assets/` is empty. I worked from the written description and the model data, and I haven't run the game or rebuilt anything, so whether the hull really stays at 100% through a launch is still untested.

**Cause:** in the `new_ground` surface starport, the invisible collision pads sit higher than the pads you see. The landing points ships are parked on are at height 72.582, exactly level with the visible pad surface. The collision pads were higher:
- pads 2–6 had their top at 72.838, 0.26 m too high;
- pad 1 had its top at 73.308, 0.73 m too high.

So a ship parked on any of these pads looks like it's resting on the surface, but its collision outline already sits partly inside the pad. When it lifts off and starts colliding again, the game counts that overlap as a crash and damages the hull. This happens on all six pads, not just the one in the video.

**Fix:** one file changed, `data/models/stations/new_ground/new_ground_landing.dae`. I set all six pads' height to the same value, so each collision top is now 72.532, 5 cm below the visible surface. I left the small gap because the collision check rejects exact contact, so two surfaces at exactly the same height could still flicker between touching and not. A ship actually coming down still hits the pads and gets docked as before, and nothing about the ship changed.

**What I checked:**
- The pads now sit below every landing point: I traced straight down from each of the six points and hit only the lowered pads. The file still parses, and only those six height numbers changed.
- Ship models aren't the cause: for the ships my script could read, the bottom of the collision shape sits at the landing point, with one possible exception (`lodos`, 7 cm lower). The script errored on one ship model before it finished the list, so a few weren't checked.
- The orbital stations' docking pads all line up with each other.

**Something else I noticed but didn't change:** in the older `ground_station` model, collision pads 09 and 13 sit 9.4 cm above their landing points, while the other twelve pads are exactly level. Small ships launching from those two pads could take the same kind of damage. It may simply be how that model was made, so I left it alone; say if you want it lowered too.
